messages:
Laura: heads-up — noticed a severe console regression after yesterday's telemetry client canary. charts take >3s to first-frame on cold load, main-thread parse spike in flamegraphs

Kevin: saw this too in EU canary, seemed tied to larger vendor chunk size? i only noticed chunk download storms in the waterfall

Jess: repro steps? i can try to grab a trace

Laura: load dashboard -> open 5 large heatmaps. cold tab on canary build. devtools network shows repeated requests for `app-vendor.XXX.js` with 200 responses but no effective caching (cache-control looks correct though)

Matt: DeployBot shows the canary: `canary/obs-client@v2.1.0` rolled at 05:12 UTC (DeployBot: link to deploy) :warning:

DeployBot: canary deployed by @sasha — rollout 10% -> 100% in 20m window

Sasha: i rolled it fast because telemetry missed a bunch of events in staging — is the telemetry client doing anything weird on boot?

Kevin: quick diff shows telem client adds an `X-Client-Trace` header on all asset fetches via the service worker fetch handler. snippet: ```js self.addEventListener('fetch', e => { e.request = new Request(e.request, { headers: { ...e.request.headers, 'X-Client-Trace': TRACE_ID } }) })``` That header will cause CDN cache-miss unless Vary handled

Jess: ahhh that would cause the browser->cdn to treat the asset as unique per-trace. even if CDN responds 200, the browser may re-request if service worker logic bypasses cache?

Laura: correct — i see identical vendor chunk requested 6 times during initial render with different trace values. main thread parse repeats because worker serves new response each time and we re-evaluate because of script execution ordering

Matt: quick mitigation option: revert the canary (roll back to obs-client@v2.0.4) — or hotfix: stop mutating request headers for navigation/static asset fetches. we can gate the header to only API routes

Sasha: i can roll back now. any objections? alternatively we could update CDN config to ignore X-Client-Trace in cache key (but that is slower and needs infra change)

Laura: rollback please. also we should add an assertion in CI that service worker doesn't add dynamic headers to cross-origin or static requests. :white_check_mark:

Kevin: logging note — we saw a related increase in tokenization CPU on client due to reparse, and console telemetry costs spiked (ops alerted)

Jess: for postmortem: include reproduction gist, exact stack traces, and a small unit test for SW fetch handler. i'll open a draft PR with tests and a small example failing request

OpsBot: Alert: CDN request rate for `app-vendor` increased 4.3x during rollout — automatically throttled, customers experienced 500/524 in some regions

Sasha: rolling back now: `deploy rollback canary/obs-client@v2.0.4` — will post when finished

DeployBot: rollback started by Sasha at 06:03 UTC — status: in-progress

Matt: follow up items: (1) add SW integration test (2) bump canary window to 1% next time (3) instrument asset cache hits in telemetry (4) patch CDN to ignore `X-Client-Trace` in cache-key if possible

Laura: adding (5) connect this to console perf dashboard so any main-thread parse spike >1s creates an alert

Jess: i'll prep the PR and include the exact repro script and perf trace link — assigning to @kevin for SW test review

Kevin: ack, will review. thanks for catching this quickly everyone :thumbsup:

Laura: sweet — thanks team. hopeful rollback clears the regression in next 10m
